title: Equal Distribution

story.briefing: The remaining charge must be split evenly between k banks, using every cell exactly once. Either it can be done or it cannot — and finding out needs pruning, not patience.
story.success: Charge distributed evenly. Every bank reads the same figure.

description: Given an array of cell charges and a bank count k, decide whether the cells can be divided into exactly k groups with identical totals. Every cell must go into exactly one group, and no group may be empty. Return true or false. If k is larger than the number of cells, the answer is false.

examples.explanation: A total of 3 cannot split into two equal groups.

hints: Two checks rule out most inputs before any searching: the total must divide evenly by k, and no single cell may exceed the target group total.
Fill one group at a time rather than assigning cells to arbitrary groups — it collapses a huge number of equivalent arrangements into one.

Sort descending and place the largest remaining cell first; a cell that fits nowhere fails immediately rather than after exploring. Track which cells are used, fill a group until it reaches the target, then start the next.
